relationships.subject: peripheral nerve injury
relationships.evidence_quote: These results indicate that nerve injury severely fragments NREMS sleep by increasing the occurrence of brief arousals during periods when sleep is fragile.

relationships.subject: Nav1.8-expressing nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: These data indicate that sleep fragmentation after nerve injury is initiated by injured peripheral Na(v)1.8-expressing nociceptors.

relationships.subject: lateral parabrachial CGRP neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: revealing that the CGRP-expressing neurons of the lateral PB are necessary for driving the fragmentation of sleep produced by peripheral nerve injury

relationships.subject: gabapentin
relationships.evidence_quote: it dose-dependently decreased the number of brief arousals during NREMS and increased NREMS episode average duration in SNI mice

relationships.subject: carbamazepine
relationships.evidence_quote: also reduced the number of brief arousals and increased NREMS continuity

key_findings: Nerve injury, but not inflammatory or chemical pain, fragments NREMS via brief arousals driven by spontaneous activity in Nav1.8/TRPV1-lineage nociceptors and relayed via lateral parabrachial CGRP neurons.
Brief arousals are reduced by gabapentin and carbamazepine, serving as a proxy for spontaneous neuropathic pain.
